dedupe_keys.name: american community survey acs 1 year and 5 year estimates tables

description: The American Community Survey (ACS) is the U.S. Census Bureau's ongoing household survey, run since 2005, that provides annual estimates on more than 40 topics about people and housing in the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico (where it is the Puerto Rico Community Survey). The tables include Detailed Tables (B and C prefixes, the most detailed estimates for all geographies down to block group), Subject Tables, four Data Profiles (social, economic, housing, demographic, down to census tract), Comparison Profiles, Ranking and Geographic Comparison Tables and Supplemental Estimates. Housing and infrastructure-relevant topics include house heating fuel, year structure built, units in structure, vehicles available, commuting mode and travel time, computer and internet use, plumbing and kitchen facilities, occupancy and tenure. Coverage: 1-year estimates for areas of 65,000 people or more; 5-year estimates for all areas down to block group. The latest releases listed on 2026-09-27 are the 2024 1-year estimates (11 September 2025) and the 2020-2024 5-year estimates (8 January 2026). Access: data.census.gov tables and maps, the Summary File, FTP and the Census Data API (free key required); free, public domain. Caveats: estimates come from a sample and carry margins of error, which are large for small areas; 1-year and 5-year estimates should not be mixed. Simulation uses: demand and exposure layers for energy, water and transport models, social vulnerability and equity weighting, and synthetic population generation. Related records: ACS PUMS microdata, ACS commuting flows, the 2020 Census DHC, the Census Data API record and the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index, which is built on ACS tables.
